_doc: What the scripts may and may not say. tools/lint-script.mjs checks every spoken line and the end-card copy against this file. 'allowed' lists the claims your product can prove today (each idea points to one by id); 'forbidden' patterns are errors, 'warn' patterns are warnings. Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched on accent-free text.

allowed.claim: [What the product really does, in one sentence you can prove]
allowed.proof: [Where it is shown: a screen, a demo, a document]

allowed.claim: [An offer that is live, with its conditions]

forbidden.why: Promised results: ad platforms reject unrealistic outcomes, and they are hard to prove.
Income or growth promises (unrealistic financial outcomes).
Asserts a personal (financial or health) situation about the viewer; say it about the situation instead.
Comparisons need proof; never name a competitor.
Time promises the product may not keep (set-up time, waiting time).
No whispered voices, ever: these direction tags make many voices whisper.

warn.why: Check the real latency or availability before saying it.
Say what is automatic and what still needs a tap.
Figures need a source you can show.
Free with which conditions? Put them on the end card (card.sub or card.fine).
Absolutes are rarely true; prefer what happens in a typical case.
